chunks: When she arrived, it was said to her: 'Is this your throne?' She said: 'It is as though it is it. We had been given knowledge before it, and we were Muslims.'
ai.seo_question: What did the Queen of Sheba say when she saw Solomon's throne?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, the Queen of Sheba’s declaration 'as if it is he' (ka annahu huwa) is interpreted as a recognition of the throne's essential reality despite its altered form, highlighting the power of divine knowledge over material appearance. Her admission that she was already 'Muslim' (submitted to God) underscores the continuity of her monotheistic faith, which she now confirms through Solomon’s miraculous sign. This moment serves as a pivotal transition from partial knowledge to full submission, illustrating the Shia emphasis on the interplay between intellect ('ilm) and devotion (islam).
